To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DEAL is the first learning-based local image descriptor that provides invariance to deformations and outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in matching deformable objects; (2) the proposed approach is general and can be extended to other tasks that involve matching non-rigid surfaces.

we propose a new method to extract local features for still images that are invariant to non-rigid deformation, which is trained end-to-end by learning to deform the object in a simulated environment.

we propose a new approach to extract local features from still images robust to non-rigidity transformations by learning a spatial transformer warper to provide invariances to rotation, scale and deformations, and that the proposed approach outperforms state of the art descriptors in different benchmarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new local feature descriptor for images that is robust to deformations and that can be applied to a wide range of applications, such as object recognition, 3D reconstruction, and image retrieval.
developing a novel approach to compute local descriptors that are robust to deformations.

our approach is the state-of-the-art method to compute local features from still images for matching objects and surfaces under non-rigid transformations.

DEAL is an end-to-end learning-based local image descriptor that is robust to non-rigidity transformations and outperforms state of the art in different datasets with real and simulated objects.
our proposed method, named DEAL, outperforms state of the art methods in different datasets with real and synthetic deformable objects, achieving the highest results in all of them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to learn a local image feature extractor which can extract features from images that are robust and invariant to deformations.
we are able to extract local descriptors for objects that are robust to deformations.
we propose to learn to deform in order to provide invariances to deformations in the image space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of simulated data can be a good alternative to real data in training learning-based descriptors.
the proposed DEAL descriptor is robust to deformations and outperforms other descriptors in different datasets.
it is possible to extract local features from images that are robust against non-rigid deformable objects and surfaces.
